summary: Introductory discovery for quick onramp to Redwood API. Ceres Crew is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a multi-tenant customer assistant product. Main concerns: time-to-first-token, latency targets (p95 < 220ms for short prompts), cost per 1k tokens, data residency and KMS integration. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot using Redwood hosted sandbox credits while benchmarking model latency. Action items captured.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit for multi-tenant SaaS
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Liam Porter (CTO, Ceres Crew), Maya Chen (Lead ML Eng), Darren Ruiz (Head of Security), Aisha Bello (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick intros?
[00:12] Liam: Yeah hi, Liam here, CTO at Ceres Crew. We're building a customer assistant embedded in partner sites, mostly short prompts and retrieval augmented replies.
[00:22] Maya: Maya, lead ML. We'll be running inference from our infra initially but exploring offload to a managed provider.
[00:27] Darren: Darren, security. I'll be focused on compliance and encryption details.
[00:32] Jordan: Great. Priya, quick pass on agenda?
[00:34] Priya: Sure, we wanna cover quickstart (credits, time-to-first-token), hosting options hosted/dedicated/private, security fit (SSO, KMS, audit logs), and next steps for a pilot. Keep it conversational.
[00:47] Liam: Sounds good. Our primary constraints — we need TTFT, that's time to first token — ideally under, um, about 200 to 250 ms p95 for short 32–64 token responses. Cost matters but latency and reliability are top.
[01:05] Priya: Right, that's helpful. Quick note: our hosted API can often hit p95 around 150–220ms depending on model and context length for short prompts. But depends on region and model choice.
[01:18] Maya: Can you clarify model choices? We currently run a trimmed transformer on A100s on prem, and we want a balance between cost and throughput.
[01:27] Priya: Yeah, we have a model catalog — open models and optimized variants. For low-latency short responses we'd recommend a quantized Llama-family variant or a smaller chat-tuned model. For throughput, Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPUs gives more predictable latency but higher fixed cost.
[01:43] Aisha: Quick Q — can we start with hosted sandbox credits while evaluating? We'd prefer to get to first token quickly.
[01:49] Jordan: Absolutely, our PLG flow gives sandbox credits and API keys — typical path is self-serve sign-up, we top-up credits, you run sample calls and we do a bench session.
[01:59] Liam: How fast can we have keys and run bench scripts?
[02:02] Priya: We can provision sandbox within a day. I'll share a lightweight benchmark harness you can run in your env or against our sandbox. It measures cold start, kv-caching effects, and streaming latency.
[02:15] Darren: That harness — does it include network emulation? We have customers in EU so latency to US regions is a concern.
[02:23] Priya: We typically recommend running in the region closest to your customer base; we have EU regions. The harness has simple RTT-aware probes but we don't do a full network emulator; you can run it behind your VPC or use our private deployment for co-located infra.
[02:38] Liam: So quick mapping — hosted for fast onramp, dedicated if we want predictable throughput, private if we need VPC/on-prem for compliance. What's the TTFT delta between hosted and dedicated?
[02:51] Priya: In many cases, hosted and dedicated are close if model and region match. Dedicated reduces multi-tenant jitter and can guarantee instance warm pools which help cold-starts. Practically for 32-token responses you might see 10–40ms improvement p95 on Dedicated. But again depends on batching and cache warmup.
[03:12] Maya: You said cache — KV cache? How does Redwood handle prefix caching? We've got repeated user context.
[03:18] Priya: Yes, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) and prefix caching. We do automatic KV reuse for identical token prefixes and recommend a cache policy based on session stickiness. That can reduce per-token compute and thus TTFT for repeat calls.
[03:34] Liam: Ok. What about cost math — for a pilot, what's the estimator for X qps and Y tokens/day?
[03:41] Jordan: We'll send a simple estimator spreadsheet. For sandbox you'll get credits; for Dedicated we can do a reserved monthly commit. We tailor recommendations based on throughput and latency SLOs.
[03:54] Aisha: Any friction around SSO/SAML for our internal admin?
[03:58] Jordan: We support SAML SSO for the Console and RBAC for token management. Darren, will you need audit log retention specifics?
[04:07] Darren: Yes, we need audit logs for one year, and evidence of SOC2 Type II. Also KMS integration — we use a cloud KMS for envelope keys and an HSM for some vaults.
[04:19] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows. For SOC2/ISO we have a security packet. We'll share the link. Some on-prem setups can use HSM integration via private deployments.
[04:33] Liam: If we start with hosted sandbox, does that mean customer data will hit Redwood systems? We need to ensure PII is not used for model training.
[04:42] Jordan: We don't use customer prompt data to train models. We have explicit policies and contractual terms for data usage; for higher assurances we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private with data isolation.
[04:55] Maya: Regarding pilot — what are realistic pilot success criteria? We propose: 1) p95 latency < 250ms for our sample prompts, 2) cost estimate meets threshold, 3) integration with our auth flow and keys.
[05:08] Priya: That sounds reasonable. For bench we typically capture p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm start, streaming percentage, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:20] Liam: Who owns running bench — us or Redwood?
[05:23] Priya: Either. We can run bench sessions with you — remote pairing — or provide the harness and you run locally. For initial run most teams run harness locally so they can emulate their network. We'll analyze results together.
[05:36] Aisha: Timeline — we want a decision in ~3 weeks to start a small pilot in prod in 2 months. Is that plausible?
[05:45] Jordan: Yes, that's doable. Week 1: sandbox + bench. Week 2: analyze results and pick hosting. Week 3–4: pilot config and commit.
[05:55] Darren: One more security nit — can you show an example audit log and sample SAML metadata?
[05:59] Priya: I'll attach example artifacts. They are redactable but show events, actor ids, tokens, and resources.
[06:08] Liam: You mentioned region parity. If we pick hosted in EU can we guarantee data residency?
[06:13] Priya: Yes, we have EU regions that keep data in-region by default for the hosted offering. For contractual data residency guarantees we often use Dedicated or Private where needed.
[06:25] Maya: About streaming vs non-streaming: our frontend prefers token streaming to reduce perceived latency. How does Redwood handle streaming in terms of cost and performance?
[06:36] Priya: Streaming is supported; cost is still per-token but streaming can reduce perceived latency on the client. There's slight overhead in maintaining open connections, but for short responses that's minimal.
[06:49] Liam: Ok. Anything about model updates or pinned versions? We need deterministic outputs for regression tests.
[06:55] Jordan: You can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts. Redwood Console exposes model versions and rollout controls. We also provide eval hooks to detect regressions against prompt sets.
[07:09] Maya: That eval hook — is that integrated into CI?
[07:12] Priya: There's an API and web hooks so you can trigger evaluations as part of CI. You upload a prompt set and thresholds and get regression alerts.
[07:22] Liam: Let's talk about a small, concrete pilot configuration we could run this week.
[07:26] Priya: Proposal: 2-week pilot using hosted sandbox credits with a target qps of 10–20 steady-state, sample prompt set of 100 prompts, run bench from EU region, capture p95, cost per 1k tokens, and streaming behavior. We'll provide keys and harness.
[07:42] Aisha: That aligns with our expectations. Any restrictions on prompt content in sandbox?
[07:47] Jordan: Standard Acceptable Use Policy applies. Sandbox is representative but short-lived. For production-grade privacy we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[07:56] Darren: On the KMS BYOK flow — if we bring our keys, how do rotation and access look operationally?
[08:03] Priya: We support periodic key rotation. Redwood only sees wrapped keys; you maintain root keys in your KMS, and we use them for envelope encryption. For Private deployments we can connect to your on-prem HSM for key operations.
[08:18] Maya: A silly question — what about open-source model variants you optimize? Any names or are those proprietary?
[08:24] Priya: We onboard curated open models and have verified performance profiles — many are community models with optimization layers. We can share a short catalog; some model names may be slightly off in transcripts (SE sometimes says Reedwood Optimized model or Redwood Opti-mize in quick speech).
[08:41] Liam: Competitors — we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI; they'd be simpler for us but cost is a consideration and we need the hosting flexibility. How does Redwood compare re: migration lock-in?
[08:55] Jordan: We design for portability — same API and model pinning, plus you can import model artifacts in private deployments. Migration overhead is lower than full bespoke infra.
[09:06] Aisha: Anything about rate limits in sandbox?
[09:09] Jordan: Sandbox has soft limits; we can raise them for pilot bench runs. For production you'll configure quotas and rate limits per token or per route.
[09:20] Samir: I'll also mention observability — Console shows per-route cost and token breakdown, trace links and per-token latency. That should help your SREs.
[09:34] Darren: Trace links — can they be forwarded to our internal tracing system?
[09:38] Priya: We have tracing hooks and can push spans to your tracing endpoint or provide links for cross-correlation.
[09:46] Maya: Ok, show of hands — remote pairing for the bench or we run offline?
[09:51] Liam: I'd prefer to run bench ourselves first and then do a pairing session.
[09:55] Priya: Works for us. We'll provide the harness and a sample script.
[09:59] Jordan: Next — paperwork. Any legal or procurement timeline items?
[10:03] Liam: If the pilot looks good we'd move to a small reserved commit. Procurement can do a standard NDA/Minimal terms quickly but security review may take longer.
[10:12] Darren: We'll need SOC2 docs, penetration test results, and an architecture diagram.
[10:18] Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and an architecture whitepaper.
[10:22] Maya: For the bench, we will provide 100 sample prompts and typical response lengths; also we'll export some traces.
[10:28] Jordan: Great. Are there any red flags or blocker items?
[10:30] Liam: The only blocker is if the p95 can't meet our ~250ms SLO in EU region. Cost we can negotiate.
[10:37] Priya: Understood. We'll prioritize the EU region bench and note caching effects.
[10:43] Aisha: Can we get a brief bulleted runbook for moving from sandbox to dedicated if pilot wins?
[10:49] Samir: I'll prepare a 1-page runbook with steps, contacts, and timeline.
[10:54] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[10:56] Darren: Encryption at rest question — default behavior for hosted?
[10:59] Priya: Data at rest is encrypted. For BYOK you still get envelope encryption under your root key.
[11:06] Liam: All right, wrap up — can we recap next steps?
[11:09] Jordan: I'll list them: provide pilot pricing + credits spreadsheet, attach SOC2/security pack and SAML examples, Priya shares harness and sample prompt set, Samir provides runbook. Customer to run bench and share traces by 2026-09-30.
[11:23] Maya: Confirmed — we'll run bench and share results.
[11:26] Liam: Good. Thanks, everyone.
[11:28] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[11:32] -- End of recorded transcript --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache; "Reedwood" for Redwood). Natural speech patterns retained.

Bench plan summary (appended):
- Pilot length: 2 weeks
- Target steady-state qps: 10–20
- Prompt set: 100 canonical prompts from Ceres Crew (customer to provide)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cold vs warm start, streaming % consumed, cost per 1k tokens
- Region: EU (provision sandbox in eu-west-1 equivalent)
- Deliverables: harness + sample script (Redwood), bench results + traces (Ceres Crew)

References shared during call:
- SOC2 pack link (to be emailed)
- Sandbox signup and credits guide (console link)
